title: Abua Awas Yojana Jharkhand: Rs 2 Lakh Pucca House Apply
meta_description: Abua Awas Yojana gives Jharkhand BPL families Rs 2 lakh to build a pucca house. Check list, apply at aay.jharkhand.gov.in. Income below Rs 2.5 lakh.

hero.one_liner: Abua Awas Yojana gives BPL families in Jharkhand Rs 2 lakh to build a pucca house, paid in installments. For families left out of PMAY-Gramin.

what_is_it: Abua Awas Yojana is Jharkhand's state-funded housing scheme that provides Rs 2 lakh to eligible BPL families for constructing a pucca (permanent) house, with the word Abua meaning 'our' or 'own' in the Mundari tribal language. The scheme's official portal is aay.jharkhand.gov.in, where the beneficiary list and payment status can be checked.

The Jharkhand government launched Abua Awas Yojana in 2023 as a complement to the central government's Pradhan Mantri Awaas Yojana Gramin (PMAY-G), targeting families who are not covered under PMAY-G due to its exclusion criteria but still genuinely lack a pucca house and live in poverty. The scheme fills the coverage gap left by central housing programs and ensures that no eligible Jharkhand family is excluded purely due to administrative or eligibility barriers.

eligibility_filters.notes: BPL families in Jharkhand not covered by PMAY-Gramin, living in kutcha houses or homeless, with land to build on. Rs 2 lakh in construction-linked installments by DBT, plus 95 days MGNREGS wages and a Rs 12,000 toilet grant. Apply at the Aapki Yojana Aapke Dwar camp or block office.

how_to_apply.title: Confirm eligibility
how_to_apply.description: Check that your family is a rural Jharkhand resident, holds a BPL ration card, has annual income below Rs 2.5 lakh, and does not own a pucca house anywhere in India. Gather documents: Aadhaar card, BPL ration card, land possession document, bank passbook, income certificate, and a self-declaration of no existing pucca house.

how_to_apply.title: Submit application at Gram Panchayat
how_to_apply.description: Visit your local Gram Panchayat office, collect the Abua Awas Yojana form, fill in all family details (income, land holding, bank account), and attach photocopies of documents. The Mukhiya or Panchayat Secretary will register your application and issue an acknowledgement receipt with a reference number.

how_to_apply.title: Wait for Gram Sabha and BDO verification
how_to_apply.description: Your application will be placed before the Gram Sabha for community verification, and the Block Development Officer will conduct a field visit to confirm you do not have a pucca house. After approval at both levels, your name is added to the sanctioned beneficiary list visible at aay.jharkhand.gov.in.

how_to_apply.title: Receive first instalment and begin construction
how_to_apply.description: Once sanctioned, the first instalment (around 40-50% of Rs 2 lakh) is transferred via DBT to your Aadhaar-linked bank account. Start construction immediately and upload geotagged photographs of the completed foundation through your Panchayat to unlock the next instalment tranche.

how_to_apply.title: Complete construction and get final instalment
how_to_apply.description: Upload photographs at the wall (lintel level) stage and again after the roof is laid; the final instalment is released once the block office issues a completion certificate confirming the 31-sq-metre pucca standard is met. Apply for MGNREGS wages on the Panchayat muster roll alongside your construction work to receive the additional 95-day labour wage benefit.

extra_sections.heading: What Abua Awas Yojana Is
content: The Rs 2 lakh financial assistance under Abua Awas Yojana is released in 2-3 instalments tied to construction progress (foundation, walls at lintel level, and roof), with geotagged photographic evidence required at each stage to unlock the next tranche. The instalment-based release mechanism ensures that construction actually happens before the full grant is disbursed, preventing funds from being diverted to other uses.

In addition to the Rs 2 lakh construction grant, Abua Awas Yojana beneficiaries are also entitled to 95 days of labour wages under MGNREGS (Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme). This MGNREGS component compensates the family for construction labour time, reducing the out-of-pocket expense for work on their own home.

The house built under Abua Awas Yojana must meet minimum state specifications: a carpet area of at least 31 square metres (approximately 333 sq ft) with three rooms plus a kitchen, built with permanent pucca materials. Brick or stone walls with a concrete or tile roof qualify as pucca; bamboo or tin sheet structures do not meet the standard.

To be eligible, a family must be a rural resident of Jharkhand holding a BPL ration card, with annual income not exceeding Rs 2.5 lakh. Additionally, the family must not own a pucca house anywhere in India; owning land in Jharkhand is not a disqualifier, but possession of a completed permanent house in any state excludes the family from the scheme.

extra_sections.heading: The Financial Help
content: The scheme targets rural residents only; urban households in Jharkhand are directed to the PMAY-U (Urban) scheme instead. Families in rural areas across all 24 districts of Jharkhand are eligible to apply, with beneficiary selection carried out at the Gram Panchayat level and verified by the Block Development Officer.

Priority in beneficiary selection under Abua Awas Yojana is given to families from vulnerable categories: Scheduled Tribes and Scheduled Castes, Particularly Vulnerable Tribal Groups (PVTGs), households headed by a widow or single woman, families affected by natural disasters or displacement, and persons with disabilities. Among otherwise eligible applicants, these categories are placed first in the order of house sanction.

The beneficiary list is published at Panchayat and district level and can also be checked online at aay.jharkhand.gov.in by searching with name, district, block, or ration card number. Being on the sanctioned list is a prerequisite for receiving the construction grant, and the list is updated periodically as new applications are verified and approved.

The application process begins at the Gram Panchayat office, where interested families submit the Abua Awas Yojana form along with required documents. Documents typically needed include the Aadhaar card, BPL ration card, land possession document, bank account passbook (for DBT), income certificate, and a self-declaration that the family does not own a pucca house anywhere in India.

extra_sections.title: A House for Families Left Out of PMAY
extra_sections.content:
Abua Awas gives eligible BPL families Rs 2 lakh to build a pucca house, paid in installments by DBT. It was launched in 2023 as a state scheme.

It is aimed at families who did not get a house under the central PMAY-Gramin, so no one is left without shelter.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: The Jharkhand government uses Awaas+ survey data and SECC 2011 (Socio-Economic and Caste Census) data to identify potential beneficiaries. Families appearing in SECC 2011 data as houseless or living in kutcha single-room structures are especially likely to be included, and the Gram Sabha verifies that selected beneficiaries genuinely lack a pucca house before names are sent forward for sanction.

Construction must be completed within 12 to 18 months from the date of sanction, or the beneficiary risks losing remaining instalments. The state's monitoring system tracks progress through geotagged photographs uploaded by Panchayat functionaries at key construction milestones, ensuring that fund releases match actual on-ground progress.

Every Abua Awas house must include a toilet under the Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) framework. Beneficiaries receive a separate SBM grant of Rs 12,000 for toilet construction in addition to the Rs 2 lakh house grant, ensuring that the completed home includes proper sanitation without placing an additional financial burden on the family.

Payment under Abua Awas Yojana is via DBT to the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account, which must be operational before the first instalment is released. The state has conducted banking camps in remote tribal areas to help families open or activate accounts so that the construction grant is not delayed by banking barriers.

extra_sections.heading: How to Apply
content: Abua Awas Yojana is distinct from PMAY-G, which is a central scheme offering Rs 1.20 lakh (plains) or Rs 1.30 lakh (hilly and northeastern areas) per house. Abua Awas provides Rs 2 lakh from Jharkhand state funds and is specifically for families who cannot access PMAY-G, meaning the two schemes together form a complementary housing coverage net for rural Jharkhand.

The PMAY-G exclusion criteria include families owning mechanised agricultural equipment, registered motor vehicles, government employees, income taxpayers, and those with a refrigerator or landline phone, among others. A significant number of genuinely poor Jharkhand families fall within these exclusion criteria, and Abua Awas Yojana was created precisely for this gap population that slips through the PMAY-G net.

Tribal families in Jharkhand have the option to use locally available stone for wall construction in hilly districts such as West Singhbhum and Saraikela-Kharsawan, where stone masonry is a traditional and structurally sound building method. The scheme does not rigidly mandate brick walls; it requires pucca-standard construction, and local stone with a concrete or corrugated steel roof qualifies in these regions.

The Jharkhand government has set lakh-level targets for houses under Abua Awas Yojana, with progress tracked through the scheme's Management Information System (MIS) on the official portal. District collectors are accountable for block-level targets, and monthly progress data is submitted to the state Rural Development Department.

extra_sections.heading: How the Installments Work
content: Under Abua Awas Yojana, the state government strongly encourages and in many cases mandates that the completed house be registered in the name of the woman of the household, or jointly in both husband's and wife's names. This asset-in-her-name policy gives women beneficiaries legal security of tenure, protecting them against displacement or domestic disputes in the future.

For families who face difficulty obtaining an income certificate or land document due to bureaucratic delays, the local Gram Panchayat Mukhiya can issue a certificate attesting to the family's houseless status, which the Block Development Officer may accept as supporting evidence during eligibility verification. The state has tried to reduce document barriers so that genuinely needy families are not excluded due to missing paperwork.

extra_sections.heading: How the Installments Work More
content: The MGNREGS labour wage component of 95 days under Abua Awas Yojana works as follows: the beneficiary family works on their own house construction and their attendance is recorded on the MGNREGS muster roll at the Panchayat level. Wages are paid at the prevailing MGNREGS daily rate (Jharkhand's MGNREGS wage rate as notified each year) and deposited into the beneficiary's Jan Dhan or MGNREGS wage bank account.

Abua Awas Yojana also operates in convergence with other Jharkhand welfare schemes: beneficiaries may simultaneously receive Maiya Samman (monthly cash for women), Sarvajan Pension (if elderly or disabled), and the Abua Swasthya Suraksha health card. This integrated welfare package means that when a poor tribal family builds their home under Abua Awas, they are not doing so in isolation but within a broader social protection framework.

extra_sections.title: Released as You Build
extra_sections.desc:
The money is not given in one go. It is released in installments linked to construction stages, from foundation to roof.

You also get 95 days of MGNREGS labour wages and a Rs 12,000 toilet grant under Swachh Bharat, on top of the Rs 2 lakh.

extra_sections.heading: Abua Awas vs PMAY-Gramin
content: The role of the Gram Sabha in Abua Awas Yojana is significant: the village assembly must formally endorse the beneficiary list before the Block Development Officer can process sanctions. This community-based verification step is designed to prevent elite capture, where relatively better-off families might otherwise manage to get their names added to housing lists through local influence or administrative connections.

Monitoring of Abua Awas Yojana is also conducted through social audits, where community members can raise concerns about exclusion errors (eligible families not on the list) or inclusion errors (ineligible families receiving the grant). The District Rural Development Agency (DRDA) handles grievances, and an online complaint mechanism at aay.jharkhand.gov.in allows families to report discrepancies from anywhere.

The quality of construction under Abua Awas Yojana is monitored by a state-level technical team that conducts random inspections of completed houses. If a house is found to fall below the required pucca construction standard (for example, using substandard materials or leaving rooms unfinished), the beneficiary may be asked to rectify the deficiency before the final instalment is released.

Abua Awas Yojana beneficiaries can also avail of a bank linkage for additional home improvement loans from rural co-operative banks or self-help group (SHG) credit programs, using the sanctioned house as collateral. The Rs 2 lakh state grant covers basic construction costs, but some families choose to top up with a small loan to add an additional room or finish the interior floors.

extra_sections.heading: Extra Support With the House
content: The Jharkhand government's Abua Awas Yojana database is integrated with the state's Jan Dhan-Aadhaar-Mobile (JAM) trinity infrastructure, which means that payment disbursal, beneficiary verification, and construction tracking are all linked to the individual's Aadhaar number. This digital integration reduces the risk of ghost beneficiaries (non-existent persons receiving funds) and makes the scheme more transparent and auditable.

Beneficiaries who belong to primitive tribal groups (PVTGs) such as the Birhor, Asur, Korwa, or Sauriya Paharia may receive additional support under the PVTG welfare framework to help them navigate the Abua Awas application process. The Tribal Welfare Department coordinates with the Rural Development Department to ensure that PVTG families, who typically have lower literacy and fewer formal documents, are not left out of the beneficiary list.

Abua Awas Yojana is part of Jharkhand's broader 'Abua' brand of welfare initiatives, which also includes the Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (Rs 15 lakh health cover) and the Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana (monthly income for women). Together, these programs represent the state government's integrated social protection vision for Jharkhand's most vulnerable communities.

Families who have previously received a housing unit under PMAY-G or any other state housing scheme are not eligible for Abua Awas Yojana for the same dwelling unit. However, if such a family has a different adult member who is houseless and living separately (for example, a married son who does not have a home), that member may apply individually if they meet all eligibility criteria as a separate household.

extra_sections.title: More Than Just the Cash
extra_sections.content:
Beyond the Rs 2 lakh, the scheme adds MGNREGS wages for 95 days of your own labour and a toilet grant under Swachh Bharat.

So the real value is higher than the headline amount, and it helps cover the labour and sanitation costs of the new home.

extra_sections.heading: Why the Scheme Matters
content: The environmental and sustainability dimension of Abua Awas Yojana is addressed through materials guidance: in cyclone-prone areas, reinforced concrete roofs are recommended over tile, and in waterlogging-prone areas, the house plinth should be raised above ground level. Block-level engineers are available to advise beneficiaries on these site-specific construction adaptations.

After a house is completed under Abua Awas Yojana, a completion photograph and georeferenced location are uploaded to the national housing dashboard, making the progress of the scheme visible at the national level. This data transparency ensures that Jharkhand's housing progress is tracked against national benchmarks and can be reviewed by central government monitoring agencies alongside PMAY-G data.

The Jharkhand government conducts awareness campaigns at the block level through ASHA workers, Anganwadi workers, and Bank Mitras to inform eligible families about the Abua Awas Yojana application window. These grassroots outreach workers are particularly important in reaching PVTG families and illiterate households who may not be aware that they are eligible or may not know how to navigate the application process.

Abua Awas Yojana houses are also expected to include provisions for rainwater harvesting and proper ventilation as part of broader sustainable construction guidelines issued by the Jharkhand Rural Development Department. While these are recommendations rather than strict construction mandates, the state's technical support team advises beneficiaries on incorporating these features into the house plan at minimal additional cost.

extra_sections.heading: Tracking Your Payments
content: For orphaned or destitute individuals who do not have a traditional family unit, the Jharkhand government has provisions to recognise such a person as an independent household unit for the purposes of Abua Awas eligibility. A single adult living alone who is houseless, earns below Rs 2.5 lakh annually, and holds a BPL ration card can apply for the scheme as a sole beneficiary household, with the Gram Panchayat certifying their houseless and destitute status.

The Abua Awas Yojana represents one of the most ambitious housing drives in Jharkhand's post-statehood history, reflecting both the scale of unmet housing need in the state and the government's intent to eradicate kutcha housing from Jharkhand within this decade. With comprehensive features including the construction grant, MGNREGS wages, toilet grant, women's ownership mandate, and rigorous digital tracking of construction progress, the scheme sets a high benchmark for how a state-level housing program can be thoughtfully designed and effectively delivered.

faqs.question: What is Abua Awas Yojana?
faqs.answer:
Abua Awas Yojana is Jharkhand's state housing scheme that provides Rs 2 lakh to BPL families in rural areas to build a pucca house of at least 31 square metres with 3 rooms and a kitchen. It targets families excluded from the central PMAY-G scheme.

The name Abua means 'our own' in the Mundari tribal language, and the official portal is aay.jharkhand.gov.in.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for Abua Awas Yojana?
faqs.answer: Rural residents of Jharkhand who hold a BPL card, have an annual family income below Rs 2.5 lakh, and do not own a pucca house anywhere in India are eligible. Priority is given to ST/SC families, women-headed households, PVTGs, disabled persons, and disaster-affected families.

faqs.question: How much money does Abua Awas Yojana give?
faqs.answer: Rs 2 lakh per family, released in instalments tied to construction progress. In addition, beneficiaries get 95 days of MGNREGS labour wages and Rs 12,000 for toilet construction under the Swachh Bharat Mission.

faqs.question: How do I check the Abua Awas Yojana beneficiary list?
faqs.answer: Visit aay.jharkhand.gov.in and search by name, district, block, or ration card number to see if your name is in the sanctioned beneficiary list. You can also check at your Gram Panchayat office.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Abua Awas Yojana and PMAY-G?
faqs.answer:
PMAY-G is a central scheme giving Rs 1.20 lakh (plains) or Rs 1.30 lakh (hills) per house with strict exclusion criteria. Abua Awas Yojana is a Jharkhand state scheme giving Rs 2 lakh and targeting families excluded from PMAY-G who still genuinely lack a pucca house.

A family cannot receive both for the same house.

faqs.question: What house specifications does Abua Awas require?
faqs.answer:
The house must have a minimum carpet area of 31 square metres with 3 rooms and a kitchen. It must be built with permanent (pucca) materials, such as brick or stone walls with a concrete or tile roof.

A toilet must also be included as part of the Swachh Bharat Mission requirement.

faqs.question: How are Abua Awas Yojana payments made?
faqs.answer: Via DBT directly to the beneficiary's Aadhaar-linked bank account in multiple instalments. Each instalment is released after geotagged photographs showing the corresponding construction stage (foundation, walls, roof) are submitted and verified.

faqs.question: Can a woman be the primary beneficiary of Abua Awas Yojana?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Women-headed households (widows, single women) are given priority under the scheme.

The policy also encourages the completed house to be registered in the woman's name or jointly in husband and wife's names to give women legal asset ownership.

faqs.question: What documents are needed to apply for Abua Awas Yojana?
faqs.answer: Typically: Aadhaar card, BPL ration card, land possession document, bank passbook (for DBT), income certificate, and a self-declaration that the family does not own a pucca house anywhere in India. Apply at your Gram Panchayat office.

faqs.question: Within how many months must the Abua Awas house be completed?
faqs.answer:
Construction must generally be completed within 12 to 18 months from the date of sanction. Failure to complete within the time limit can result in cancellation of remaining instalments.

The block office tracks progress through geotagged photographs uploaded at each construction stage.
